details:
An image format based on the relatively "new" AV1 video codec, AVIF supports a wide range of bit depths and export options, including lossless encoding that beats PNG by (in some cases) over 70% file size reduction, and HDR imaging.

I've long put off the idea of loading images from the Virtual Furry Museum through the image downloader on a few counts: No compressed BC7 support, which means results are either VRAM-hungry RGB24, or very poor-quality 4-bit-per-texel DXT1. And 2, very large file sizes on download, if the images were lossless or very high quality. 3, limitations on downloading individual images in quick succession, and 4, resolution limits to 2K.

But now that I'm making a presentation system based on the image downloader, I'm seeing the efficiency of WebP at compressing lossless with significantly better memory savings than very high lossy. That got me very excited to investigate new formats some more.

I take so many pictures in VRChat as 4K PNGs, but PNG for all these is way too hefty. An AVIF or WebP option for the camera/screenshot tool would be phenomenal!

On the Image Downloader side, supporting AVIF in tandem with BC7 would accomplish two things: extremely small file downloads over networks, and high-quality compressed textures with minimal artifacts. If the tool supported this, I'd consider using it in the museum for sure.

NOTE: while DXT1 on-the-fly encoding is possible today in Udon by getting the results and compressing from a Texture2D, I think expanding these options in the Texture Info data type directly would make the tool much easier to use. Or, if Udon could somehow allow BC7 encoding, that'd be really great!
title: AVIF Import and DXT1/BC7 Encoding Support for VRCImageDownloader and Screenshots
